A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Kontinuous Kontext. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rearrangement.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark comparisons, architectural and filtering ablations, user studies, and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds trajectory diagnostics, compositional editing demonstrations and latency measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 substantially revises the stated projector architecture from 1536 -> 256 -> 128 -> 6192 to 1536 -> 6144 -> 6144 -> 6144 -> 6144, with modulation-output halves changing from 3096 to 3072. The conditioning mechanism, LoRA training and flow-matching objective remain. The PDFs do not establish whether this architectural revision corrects earlier documentation or describes a newly trained variant.

E1.justification: V2 adds sequential, two-instruction editing with independently controlled strengths in A.11 and Figure 28, extending beyond v1's single-pass editing demonstrations. The existing training sources, PIEBench evaluation and domain-specific coverage remain. A.12 discusses other architectures without evaluating them.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain Diffmorpher, Freemorph, WAN-2.1, ConceptSliders, MARBLE, CFG-scale and attention reweighting. The new computational-cost table uses existing comparators; Flux Kontext was already the base-model latency reference in v1.

E3.justification: V2 adds DINO-based evaluation, Pearson-correlation linearity scoring, CLIP-direction versus LPIPS tradeoff analysis, sequential editing tests and explicit latency measurement. Existing benchmark and user-study sample sizes remain. The auxiliary 10K size-change dataset is described as zooming rather than black-background compositing, although an actual preprocessing change is not established.

E4.justification: V2 extends the supplementary analyses with DINO identity/linearity diagnostics, faithfulness-versus-identity tradeoffs, compositional case studies and computational-cost analysis. The existing conditioning, text-input and filtering ablations, smoothness-metric validation and extrapolation failures are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 9 newly reports absolute Pearson correlations to summarize trajectory linearity, adding a statistical analysis absent from v1. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; the addition does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: The benchmark and ablation table values remain unchanged after matching split tables. However, Figure 17 revises the proposed method's CLIP identity curve against ConceptSliders: its full-strength endpoint changes from approximately 0.78 to 0.82. V2 also adds linearity results, including |r| = 0.985, latency of 60 seconds versus 56 seconds for Flux Kontext, and added/replaced qualitative examples. These do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The strength-grid definition, flow-matching loss, first- and second-order smoothness definitions, and normalized CLIP-direction formula are retained. V2 adds empirical metrics and conceptual discussion, without new formal assumptions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: unified continuous edit-strength control through a text-conditioned modulation projector, trained using filtered synthetic trajectories without attribute-specific training. Additional evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of linearity and faithfulness/identity tradeoffs, and explicitly argues compatibility with other DiT-based editors in A.12 without testing that generalization. Geometric-editing and extrapolation limitations remain; the discrete-edit boundary is still stated elsewhere despite its removal from the conclusion.

D1.justification: A.1 changes the reported training resources from one A100 and 120 hours to eight A100s and 72 hours, alongside the substantial projector specification revision. V2 newly explains threshold selection using approximately 100 sequences per category and supplies latency and parameter-cost details. Conversely, it removes the project link and explicit promise to release code, models and raw/filtered datasets; actual resource availability cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to DINOv2, IP-Adapter and Huang and Belongie's adaptive-normalization work, while retaining the main related-work organization and novelty positioning. Its additional StyleGAN-NADA bibliography entry represents an already cited work rather than a new research connection.

P1.justification: The five main sections and most prose remain, with copyediting and expanded filtering explanations. V2 introduces a supplementary-material heading and contents, reorganizes appendix subsections, moves references to the end, and removes the standalone reproducibility and ethics statements. Some cross-references become inconsistent, including the conclusion's appendix Figure 4 reference to the failure example actually numbered Figure 27.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: the dataset gallery moves to the appendix, the architecture figure and baseline table are split, and gallery panels are moved or replaced. It adds DINO and tradeoff plots, compositional-edit grids and a cost table, while resizing and relocating many existing displays. These changes extend well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens the evidence for controllability through DINO-linearity and faithfulness/identity analyses, compositional demonstrations and explicit computational costs. Threshold-selection details also help reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by unexplained architecture/training specification revisions, removed release information and inconsistent appendix references. The unchanged main tables and unexplained identity-curve revision do not establish a new performance gain.
